items.body_md:
On August 7, an unnamed movant filed the relief from stay motion at Dkt. 146 — the sole substantive entry in this case over the 72-hour lookback — with no response yet appearing on the docket as of this briefing. The full text of Dkt. 146 has not been pulled, so the movant's identity, the specific asset or claim at issue, and the precise relief requested remain unverified. That gap continues to be the threshold analytical problem: without the document, the motion cannot be sized against the estate or mapped to any creditor class's recovery. Confirmation would require a PACER pull of Dkt. 146. Under S.D. Tex. Bankruptcy Local Rule 4001-1, a response is due 14 days from service; service was completed by the BNC certificate at Dkt. 158, filed August 8, placing the response deadline on or about August 22.

The sequencing is consequential. August 22 falls two days before the second-day hearing before Judge Lopez on August 24, which means Dkt. 146 is likely to land on the August 24 docket in one of three postures: fully contested if a timely response is filed; resolved by agreed order if the parties settle the motion before the hearing; or deemed unopposed and subject to grant if no response appears. A contested or granted motion touching estate property — inventory, a receivable, a leased facility — removes that asset from the distributable pool before any 363 sale process has run its course. Given that RNDC's disclosed asset range of $500 million to $1 billion in assets sits well below its $1 billion to $10 billion in liabilities, any pre-confirmation erosion of estate property carries direct consequences for the approximately 100,000 unsecured creditors owed more than $400 million per court filings reported by __[The Drinks Business](https://www.thedrinksbusiness.com/2026/08/rndc-court-filings-reveal-scale-of-distributors-financial-collapse/)__.

Dkts. 147–155 and 158 — pro hac vice admissions, notices of appearance, supporting affidavits, and the BNC certificate of mailing — are procedural and routine and carry no independent weight here. The press record through this morning shows no new reporting beyond what has been covered in prior editions. The Disclosure Statement filed at Dkt. 118 on August 4 remains pending court approval and is not yet soliciting votes; no plan supplement or amended plan has appeared on the docket. The next concrete milestone is the second-day hearing before Judge Lopez on August 24, 2026, which is expected to carry first-day-to-final order conversions, the Official Committee of Unsecured Creditors' first formal appearance on the record, and — depending on whether a response to Dkt. 146 is filed by August 22 — the lift-stay motion itself.
